HAIM moves detection beyond binary "AI-or-human" toward **role-level tracking** (Composer / Lyricist / Vocalist / Audio Engineer), with **153,686 tracks** (67,000 with audio ≈ 229 GB + 86,686 link-based) across **13 categories** that isolate each stage of AI intervention. > **The viewer configs above are 100-row samples for preview/listening only** — `load_dataset(...)` returns these samples, **not** the full dataset. > The complete data lives in the **raw folders** (`A_full_generation/`, `B_hybrid/`, `C_mixing/`) — see [Download the full dataset](#quick-start-download-the-full-dataset). ## Preview In the Data Studio above, pick a config (e.g. `B_hybrid_audio_preview`) → a split (e.g. `B1_ai_mastered_human`) → press ▶ to listen. The classic real-vs-fake axis, at scale and multi-platform. **B — Hybrid production.** The interesting middle: AI mastering on human tracks (B1), human mastering/mixing on AI tracks (B2–B4), AI vocal covers on human tracks (B5), AI generation conditioned on human-written lyrics (B6), and AI variation / edit / repaint of real songs (B7–B9). # ArtifactBench v1 — AI-Generated Music Detection Benchmark

A multi-generator evaluation benchmark for AI-generated music forensic detection, covering 22 AI generators and 6 real music sources.

**From benchmark to a real file:** [run the live ArtifactNet demo](https://demo.intrect.io/?utm_source=huggingface&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=artifactnet_hub_2026q3&utm_content=dataset_card), or read the [production detector's scope and limitations](https://intrect.io/artifactnet/?utm_source=huggingface&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=artifactnet_hub_2026q3&utm_content=dataset_card). No account is required for the first demo analysis.

## Dataset Description

- **Total tracks**: 8,766 (4,383 AI + 4,383 Real, 1:1 balanced)
- **AI generators**: 22 (MusicGen, Stable Audio, Suno v3/v3.5/v4, Udio, Riffusion, DiffRhythm, Yue, Chirp v2/v3/v3.5, etc.)
- **Real sources**: 6 (SONICS, MoM, FMA, YouTube)
- **Format**: AI tracks as Parquet (audio bytes embedded), Real tracks as CSV (YouTube IDs for user download)

## Motivation

Existing benchmarks (SONICS: 5 generators, MoM: 6 generators) only measure in-distribution performance. Models reporting high F1 on these benchmarks fail catastrophically on out-of-distribution generators:

- CLAM (194M params, F1=0.925 on MoM) → F1=0.824 on ArtifactBench
- SpecTTTra (19M params, F1=0.97 on SONICS) → F1=0.766 on ArtifactBench

ArtifactBench evaluates what matters for deployment: generalization across diverse generators.

## Sanity Check Protocol

Per-source pass/fail thresholds:
- Real source FPR ≤ 5%
- AI source TPR ≥ 90% (Stable Audio: ≥ 60%)
- Codec invariance: mean Δ ≤ 0.15, max Δ ≤ 0.35

## Baseline Results

| Model | Params | F1 | FAIL | Suno v4 TPR | Real FPR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ArtifactNet v9.4** | **4.2M** | **0.983** | **4/28** | **98%** | **1.5%** |
| CLAM (MoM) | 194M | 0.824 | 16/28 | 78% | 70.5% |
| SpecTTTra | 19M | 0.766 | 23/28 | 55% | 21.4% |

## Public Model Comparison — 8-way (v1.1 test partition, 2026-07-04)

Eight publicly-available detectors scored on identical files with the same runner
(adapters in `artifactbench/models/`), τ = 0.5. n = 2,104 (1,388 AI / 716 real —
the locally-restored real set; see the provenance caveat in `v1.1/RESULTS_8WAY.md`).

|---|---|---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|

# MuseBench: Sample Dataset for Distinguishing Human vs. AI-Generated Music

This repository contains a **sample preview** of the MuseBench dataset used for benchmarking human-vs-AI music classification. Each folder includes a single representative file so users can inspect the layout before downloading the full release. The complete dataset is hosted on Hugging Face under [Anonymousv22222](https://huggingface.co/Anonymousv22222), split across `MuseBench-part1` … `MuseBench-part5` (see the [Download](#download) section below).

---

## Overview

MuseBench pairs **real human-made music** with **AI-generated counterparts** from 10 different text-to-music / music-generation systems, then augments the AI side with **8 perturbation / codec variants** for robustness benchmarking. It also ships an out-of-distribution (OOD) human-music split and an AI–human co-created split.

| Split | Source | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Human (in-distribution) | `Jamendo/` — sampled from [JamendoMaxCaps](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amaai-lab/JamendoMaxCaps) | ~9,945 tracks |
| Human (out-of-distribution) | `OOD FMA/` — Free Music Archive 2008-2010 | ~8,673 tracks |
| AI-generated (paired)   | 8 generators × {Genius-Lyrics caption set, Jamendo} | `*_generated_music/` |
| AI-generated (standalone)| Suno + Udio | ~10K each |
| AI perturbations | 8 processing variants × 10 generators | see below |
| AI–human co-creation | `ai_human_co-created_music/Jamendo/` | mixed-authorship audio |

> The **Genius-Lyrics source audio is not redistributed** here (copyrighted commercial recordings); only AI generations conditioned on its captions are included. The Jamendo source audio *is* shipped, re-distributed from [JamendoMaxCaps](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amaai-lab/JamendoMaxCaps) (dataset license: **CC-BY-SA 3.0**). Per-track audio retains its original Jamendo license — typically CC-BY, CC-BY-SA, CC-BY-NC, or CC-BY-NC-ND — recorded in each track's `license_ccurl` metadata field.

---

## Download

The full MuseBench release is distributed as **5 parts × 15 tar shards each** (75 tar files in total, ~800 GB combined). Each part lives in its own Hugging Face repository to keep download sizes manageable. Download all parts and extract every shard into the same root directory to reconstruct the dataset.

| Part | Repository | # Shards | Size |
|------|------------|----------|------|
| Sample preview | [Anonymousv22222/MuseBench-Example](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anonymousv22222/MuseBench-Example) | (single tree) | ~287 MB |
| Part 1 | [Anonymousv22222/MuseBench-part1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anonymousv22222/MuseBench-part1) | `part1_001.tar` … `part1_015.tar` | ~159 GB |
| Part 2 | [Anonymousv22222/MuseBench-part2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anonymousv22222/MuseBench-part2) | `part2_001.tar` … `part2_015.tar` | ~160 GB |
| Part 3 | [Anonymousv22222/MuseBench-part3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anonymousv22222/MuseBench-part3) | `part3_001.tar` … `part3_015.tar` | ~160 GB |
| Part 4 | [Anonymousv22222/MuseBench-part4](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anonymousv22222/MuseBench-part4) | `part4_001.tar` … `part4_015.tar` | ~161 GB |
| Part 5 | [Anonymousv22222/MuseBench-part5](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anonymousv22222/MuseBench-part5) | `part5_001.tar` … `part5_015.tar` | ~160 GB |

Within each part, shards `*_001.tar` through `*_014.tar` are ~10.7 GB; the final shard `*_015.tar` is the smaller remainder (~8.8 – 9.97 GB).

After downloading, extract every tar shard into the same directory:

```bash
for f in part*_*.tar; do tar -xf "$f"; done
```

This reconstructs the full directory tree described below.

---

## Dataset Structure

After extracting all parts, the directory tree mirrors the layout of the [MuseBench-Example](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anonymousv22222/MuseBench-Example/tree/main) preview repository:

```
MuseBench/
├── Jamendo/                             # Real human (in-distribution) — flat .mp3 from JamendoMaxCaps
├── OOD FMA/                             # Real human (out-of-distribution) — flat .mp3, FMA pre-2008
│
├── MagNet_Generated_Music/              # Paired AI generations (one .wav per source track)
│   ├── Genius-Lyrics/                   #   conditioned on Genius caption set
│   └── Jamedo/                          #   conditioned on Jamendo
├── Musicgen_Generated_Music/            # (same Genius-Lyrics / Jamedo split as above)
├── audioldm_generated_music/
├── jasco_generated_music/               #   uses lowercase `Genius-lyrics/`
├── magenta_generated_music/
├── mustango_generated_music/
├── riffusion_generated_music/
├── stable_audio_generated_music/
│
├── suno_generated_music/                # Standalone AI tracks (no paired real source)
│   └── fake_XXXXX_suno_{0,1}.mp3
├── udio_generated_music/                # Standalone AI tracks
│   └── fake_XXXXX_udio_{0,1}.mp3
│
├── ai_human_co-created_music/           # AI–human collaborative tracks
│   └── Jamendo/
│
├── aac_generated_music/                 # Robustness variants — each contains 10 generator subfolders
│   ├── MagNet_Generated_Music/          # (MagNet, Musicgen, audioldm, jasco, magenta,
│   ├── Musicgen_Generated_Music/        #  mustango, riffusion, stable_audio, suno, udio)
│   └── ...                              # → AI tracks re-encoded as AAC
├── eq_generated_music/                  # → AI tracks with EQ applied
├── gaussion_noised_music/               # → AI tracks with additive Gaussian noise
├── loudness_generation_music/           # → AI tracks with loudness modification
├── mp3_noised_music/                    # → AI tracks transcoded through MP3
├── ogg_noised_music/                    # → AI tracks transcoded through OGG
├── pgd_generated_music/                 # → AI tracks with PGD adversarial perturbation
└── pitch_time_generated_music/          # → AI tracks with pitch / time-stretch
```

For each paired AI generator (MagNet, MusicGen, AudioLDM, JASCO, Magenta, Mustango, Riffusion, Stable Audio), the generated file shares the **base name of its source track** with `.wav` appended (e.g. `10 Bands_Drake_tcL2B0ilMZw.mp3.wav`). This makes it trivial to align human ↔ AI pairs across folders, and to align an AI track with its perturbed version (same filename, different parent folder).

> **Folder-spelling notes:** the Jamendo subfolder under each generator is `Jamedo/` (single 'n') — preserved as-is from the original generation pipeline. JASCO additionally uses lowercase `Genius-lyrics/`.
>
> **No top-level Genius-Lyrics audio:** the original Genius-Lyrics human recordings are copyrighted commercial tracks and are *not* redistributed here. Only the AI tracks conditioned on those captions are shipped (under each generator's `Genius-Lyrics/` subfolder).

---

## Real Human Music

### Jamendo (`Jamendo/`)
~10K tracks sampled from the [JamendoMaxCaps](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amaai-lab/JamendoMaxCaps) dataset, which sources audio from [Jamendo](https://www.jamendo.com/), where artists publish under [Creative Commons licenses](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/). Per-track licenses vary (CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC BY-NC, etc.); for any commercial use refer to [Jamendo Licensing](https://licensing.jamendo.com/).

### Out-of-Distribution FMA (`OOD FMA/`)
Tracks from the **2008-2010** window drawn from the [Free Music Archive (FMA)](https://github.com/mdeff/fma). Used as a held-out human-music distribution to test generalization. The FMA metadata is CC BY 4.0; individual audio files inherit each artist's chosen Creative Commons license.

### Genius-Lyrics (not redistributed)
The Genius-Lyrics caption set was used to **condition** AI generators (so each `*_generated_music/Genius-Lyrics/` folder contains AI outputs paired with that caption set), but the **original human recordings are not shipped** — they are commercial copyrighted tracks. To reproduce the human side of this split, source the audio yourself from the original Genius / YouTube identifiers used during generation.

---

## AI-Generated Music

For each track in the Genius-Lyrics caption set and the Jamendo split, eight open / publicly described generators produce a parallel track. Outputs live under `*_generated_music/{Genius-Lyrics, Jamedo}/`.

| Generator | Folder | Conditioning | Output Format | Model License |
|-----------|--------|--------------|---------------|---------------|
| [MusicGen](https://github.com/facebookresearch/audiocraft) | `Musicgen_Generated_Music/` | Text + optional melody | `.wav` | Code: MIT · Weights: CC-BY-NC 4.0 |
| [MAGNeT](https://github.com/facebookresearch/audiocraft) | `MagNet_Generated_Music/` | Text | `.wav` | Code: MIT · Weights: CC-BY-NC 4.0 |
| [AudioLDM](https://github.com/haoheliu/AudioLDM) | `audioldm_generated_music/` | Text | `.wav` | CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0 |
| [JASCO](https://github.com/facebookresearch/audiocraft) | `jasco_generated_music/` | Text + chords / melody / drums | `.wav` | Code: MIT · Weights: CC-BY-NC 4.0 |
| [Magenta](https://github.com/magenta/magenta) | `magenta_generated_music/` | Symbolic / text | `.wav` | Apache 2.0 |
| [Mustango](https://github.com/AMAAI-Lab/mustango) | `mustango_generated_music/` | Text + music-theory controls | `.wav` | CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0 |
| [Riffusion](https://huggingface.co/riffusion/riffusion-model-v1) | `riffusion_generated_music/` | Text (via spectrogram diffusion) | `.wav` | MIT (CreativeML OpenRAIL-M for the SD base) |
| [Stable Audio Open](https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-audio-open-1.0) | `stable_audio_generated_music/` | Text | `.wav` | Stability AI Community License (research / non-commercial) |

In addition, two **closed-source commercial** generators contribute standalone fakes (no paired real reference):

| Generator | Folder | # Tracks | License Notes |
|-----------|--------|----------|---------------|
| [Suno](https://suno.com) | `suno_generated_music/` | ~10K | Outputs governed by [Suno Terms of Service](https://suno.com/terms-of-service); included here under research/fair-use grounds |
| [Udio](https://www.udio.com) | `udio_generated_music/` | ~10K | Outputs governed by Udio's Terms of Service; included for research purposes only |

Naming convention for the standalone splits: `fake_<ID>_<generator>_<seed>.mp3` (e.g. `fake_00012_udio_1.mp3`).

---

## Robustness / Perturbation Variants

To benchmark detector robustness, every AI track (across all 10 generators above, including Suno and Udio) is also re-released under 8 audio perturbations. Each variant folder mirrors the 10-generator subfolder layout, and filenames inside each generator subfolder match those of the unperturbed AI track — so a detector can be evaluated head-to-head on `clean ↔ perturbed` pairs.

| Variant folder | Perturbation |
|----------------|--------------|
| `aac_generated_music/` | AAC re-encoding (lossy codec round-trip) |
| `mp3_noised_music/`    | MP3 transcoding artifacts |
| `ogg_noised_music/`    | OGG transcoding artifacts |
| `eq_generated_music/`  | Equalization filtering |
| `loudness_generation_music/` | Loudness normalization / amplitude scaling |
| `pitch_time_generated_music/` | Pitch shift + time stretch |
| `gaussion_noised_music/` | Additive Gaussian noise |
| `pgd_generated_music/` | PGD adversarial perturbation |

---

## AI–Human Co-Created Music

`ai_human_co-created_music/Jamendo/` contains tracks where AI generation and human edits / performance are mixed. Useful as a "gray zone" split for evaluating detectors that may otherwise treat human vs. AI as binary.

---

## Intended Use

This sample is intended for:

- Training and evaluating **human-vs-AI music detectors**.
- Benchmarking robustness across multiple text-to-music generators.
- **Robustness testing** against codec re-encoding, EQ, loudness, pitch/time, additive noise, and PGD adversarial perturbation.
- Evaluating detectors on **gray-zone** AI–human co-created music.
- Studying caption-conditioned generation quality.
- Analyzing distribution shift via the OOD-FMA split.

It is **not** intended for training commercial generative models or for any use that would conflict with the underlying source licenses listed above.

# JamendoMaxCaps Dataset

[![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2502.07461-brightgreen.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.07461)

JamendoMaxCaps is a large-scale dataset of over 362,000 instrumental tracks sourced from the [Jamendo](https://www.jamendo.com/) platform. It includes generated music captions and original metadata. Additionally, we introduce a retrieval system that utilizes both musical features and metadata to identify similar songs, which are then used to impute missing metadata via a local large language model (LLLM). 

This dataset facilitates research in:
- Music-language understanding
- Music retrieval and representation learning
- AI-generated music applications

For details on the retrieval system and metadata imputation, visit our **[GitHub repository](https://github.com/AMAAI-Lab/JamendoMaxCaps)**.

## Dataset Details

The dataset is stored in **parquet format** within the `data` folder. Each entry contains:
- **`array`**: The audio file stored as an array.
- **`path`**: The unique identifier for the MP3 file (`<unique_id>.mp3`).

### Extracting MP3 Files
To convert the stored audio arrays into MP3 files, use the following script:

```python
import os
import soundfile as sf
from datasets import load_dataset

def read_jamendo_max():
    dataset = load_dataset("amaai-lab/JamendoMaxCaps", data_dir="data")
    return dataset

def save_mp3_files(dataset, output_dir="mp3_files"):
    os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
    
    for example in dataset['train']:
        audio = example['audio']['array']
        sample_rate = example['audio']['sampling_rate']
        path = example['audio']['path']
        output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, path)
        
        sf.write(output_path, audio, sample_rate, format='MP3')
        print(f"Saved file: {output_path}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    dataset = read_jamendo_max()
    save_mp3_files(dataset)
```

### Metadata
Original metadata is provided in **multiple JSONL files** for easy handling. Each entry follows this structure:

```json
{
  "id": "882977",
  "name": "A Singleness of Intention 04",
  "duration": 154,
  "artist_id": "362132",
  "artist_name": "Matthew VandenBrook",
  "album_name": "A Singleness of Intention",
  "album_id": "103795",
  "license_ccurl": "http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/3.0/",
  "releasedate": "2011-12-18",
  "audio": "https://prod-1.storage.jamendo.com/?trackid=882977&format=mp31",
  "audiodownload": "https://prod-1.storage.jamendo.com/download/track/882977/mp32/",
  "musicinfo": {
    "vocalinstrumental": "instrumental",
    "speed": "medium",
    "tags": {
      "genres": [],
      "instruments": [],
      "vartags": []
    }
  },
  "audiodownload_allowed": true
}
```
- **`id`**: Unique identifier for each song.
- **`musicinfo`**: Contains attributes like **instrumental/vocal classification** and **tempo (e.g., medium speed)**.
- **`audio`** & **`audiodownload`**: Links to the track's online and downloadable versions.

### Captions
We provide captions for **30-second segments** using [Qwen2-Audio](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen2-Audio). Captions are stored in `final_caption30sec.jsonl`. Example:

```json
{
  "start_time": 60.0,
  "end_time": 90.0,
  "caption": "The music is a fast-paced electronic track in F# minor with a tempo of 84 BPM featuring heavy drum beats and a complex chord progression. The genre includes breakbeat, drum and bass, easy listening, electronic, IDM, and lounge. It creates an energetic mood and could be suitable for a mobile car racing game soundtrack.",
  "id": "1176956"
}
```
